summary: Prompt human review is supported for a sensitive goals-of-care conversation alongside active disease management. The record shows progressive congestion symptoms followed by an urgent attendance for acute decompensated heart failure, IV diuresis, and residual cardiorenal vulnerability at discharge. Improvement with treatment is reassuring but does not remove the value of discussing priorities, acceptable care, and escalation preferences; the record does not document an active advance-care plan.

summaryEvidence.detail: Home visit documented nocturnal breathlessness, slower walking, mild bilateral ankle oedema, weight 84.1 kg, oxygen saturation 94%, and respiratory rate 20.
Urgent hospital attendance documented orthopnoea, rapid weight gain, bilateral crackles, radiographic vascular congestion, and initiation of IV loop diuresis.
Discharge summary documented improved breathing after IV diuresis but renal function below usual baseline, with heart-failure and renal follow-up requested.

evidenceForReview.significance: Ankle oedema and weight gain progressed to nocturnal breathlessness, slower walking, orthopnoea, and an urgent acute-care presentation, supporting timely review of priorities as well as clinical treatment.

evidenceForReview.significance: Renal deterioration and potassium elevation can constrain heart-failure treatment and increase the importance of coordinated planning and clear escalation arrangements.

evidence.detail: Renal and congestion report recorded creatinine 98 µmol/L, eGFR 58 mL/min/1.73m², potassium 5.5 mmol/L, NT-proBNP 3560 ng/L, and same-week heart-failure assessment.
Discharge summary stated renal function remained below baseline and potassium required surveillance.

alternativeExplanations: The acute symptoms were attributable to fluid overload and improved after IV diuresis.
Post-discharge renal blood results showed creatinine 65 µmol/L, eGFR 75 mL/min/1.73m², and potassium 5.0 mmol/L, which may indicate partial recovery from the acute cardiorenal disturbance.

The record supports continued active heart-failure and renal management; goals-of-care review should not displace the requested clinical follow-up.
